validity.researcher_notes: The Operator cell lists three companies joined by semicolons. Owner2 is Gazprom PJSC, while a Gazprom subsidiary in Yekaterinburg holds the Russian section. No page in the wiki list states the three owners on the sheet.

fills.researcher_notes: The cdu.ru article on Kazakhstan gas transit lists the Soyuz pipeline at 25.2 billion cubic meters a year, the sheet value. Russian Wikipedia and a Sputnik Tajikistan article of 23 February 2021 give 26 billion cubic meters a year as the design figure, so the sources differ by 0.8. The sheet value stays, with the 26 noted.

Russian Wikipedia gives a diameter of 1420 mm for the Soyuz pipeline. Ukrainian Wikipedia says the Soyuz line was built in 1978 as two strings of 1420 mm, with a capacity of up to 26 billion cubic meters a year. Both are secondary pages and trace to the same Soviet-era description, so they are not counted as independent.

Russian Wikipedia says operation began on 11 November 1980 (built 1975 to 1979). A Sputnik Tajikistan article of 23 February 2021 says the same date. The sheet start year of 1980 matches. The start month, 11, is stated on both pages.

An Enerdata executive briefing of 24 July 2023 says that after 10 May 2022 Gazprom closed the main Soyuz pipeline and with it transit through the Sokhranivka entry point. This supports a pipeline that is shut but not removed. A Sputnik Tajikistan article of 23 February 2021 reports an earlier transit stop after an explosion on Soyuz. A Reuters article cited by the wiki could not be read this pass.

The harvested pages that describe operators (the Gas Transmission System Operator of Ukraine page on LinkedIn, the Intergas Central Asia site) describe whole national networks and do not name the Soyuz pipeline, so they are not a ref for this row. A Sputnik Tajikistan article of 23 February 2021 says the Russian section belongs to Gazprom Transgaz Yekaterinburg. No wiki citation states the three-operator value on the sheet; not searched this pass.

No harvested page that names Soyuz states the three owners on the sheet. The Ukrainian and Kazakh company pages describe whole networks. A Sputnik Tajikistan article of 23 February 2021 says the Russian section belongs to Gazprom Transgaz Yekaterinburg, a Gazprom subsidiary, which would be the lower-level owner of that section. No wiki citation states the sheet value; not searched this pass.
